title: Introduce tenanted pacekeeper + soft rejoin probe to smooth regional rejoin spikes
author: Maya Patel
body: Motivation: We observed transient regional latency spikes and downstream SLO oscillations during rapid regional rejoin events when large numbers of tenant connections returned after an isolate window. This PR introduces a tenanted 'pacekeeper' token-based gating layer plus a soft-rejoin probe that staggers KV warmups and prevents a sharp surge hitting the fast-path. Design summary: The pacekeeper maintains per-tenant windows that limit concurrent fast-path sessions and releases tokens at a measured rate derived from recent successful token consumption and observed P95 latency. The soft rejoin probe runs as part of connection restoration: rather than immediately reattaching a tenant to the regular serving module, the probe exercises a lightweight probe RPC which warms KV cache prefixes and verifies end-to-end tail latency under a capped load before full rejoin. Key features: 1) Token bucket per tenant with exponential decay of peak allowance; 2) Probe RPC with success/fail counters and backoff that feeds into the tenant token rate; 3) Metrics and traces for token availability, token denial rate, probe pass rate, and observed incremental KV hit ratio; 4) Configurable emergency-bypass policy for enterprise customers (safety valve in case of false positives). Backwards compatibility: Pacekeeper operates as a local middleware layer in the serving runtime and is off by default for legacy tenants. We provide a rollout flag that starts in canary for the 'tenanted' rollout group. Tests and validation: Unit tests for token lifecycle, decay scheduler, and probe state machine. Integration test harness simulates 10k tenants rejoining in a 30s window and asserts that fast-path QPS spikes are reduced by at least 70% while average P95 increases less than 10ms. Load tests executed in benchmark-lab region with a shadowing run for 1 hour. Observability: Added 4 new traces and 6 metrics: pacekeeper.tokens.available, pacekeeper.tokens.denied, rejoin_probe.pass_rate, rejoin_probe.latency_p95, tenant_kv_prefix_warm_ratio, tenant_rejoin_delay_dist. Rollout and rollback plan: Deploy behind feature flag on canary (5% of traffic) for 2 hours, monitor metrics and alert on a >5% increase in request error rate or >20% increase in P99 latency for the canary cohort. If triggered, toggle emergency-bypass which immediately drains pacekeeper and allows immediate rejoin. Commits summary: - Add pacekeeper middleware and token store with decay scheduler - Implement soft rejoin probe RPC and state machine - Wire metrics/traces and small console dashboard config - Add unit and integration tests + benchmark harness scenario - Add canary rollout flag and emergency-bypass gate Files changed (high level): src/runtime/pacekeeper.rs (token lifecycle & scheduler), src/runtime/rejoin_probe.rs (probe state machine & RPC client), src/runtime/mod.rs (middleware wiring), charts/console/pacing_dashboard.yaml (dashboard tiles), integration-tests/rejoin_storm_scenario.py (load harness), docs/operational/pacekeeper.md (how to interpret metrics and rollback), infra/featureflags.yaml (canary config), tests/unit/test_pacekeeper.rs (unit tests), tests/integration/test_rejoin_probe.py (integration assertions). Review conversation summary: - Ethan Brooks: "Can we add a per-tenant opt-out flag for compliance customers?" Author: "Added emergency-bypass and an allowlist config; also documented behavior in docs/operational/pacekeeper.md." - Lina Gomez: "Concerned about the token decay math under heavy churn; can we add a stress test?" Author: "Added a 10k-tenant churn scenario to benchmark-lab and uploaded results to the Linear ticket ENG-4621." - Markus Huber: "Looks good, one nit on metric naming and a minor race in token refill." Author: "Fixed metric prefix and added an atomic refill routine; pushed a follow-up commit." CI and checks: - unit-tests: pass - integration-tests (short): pass - lint: pass - benchmark-lab-shadow: pass - e2e: pass Merge notes: Squash merge after final CI green. Release notes: "Introduce tenanted pacekeeper to smooth regional rejoin traffic spikes; enables configurable emergency-bypass and observability for troubleshooting. Improves resilience during large-scale regional restores." Additional context: This PR was implemented as a response to an incident on 2026-02-11 where a region rejoin produced a transient 3x tail-latency spike affecting hosted customers. The approach emphasizes graceful ramping and observability over hard denials; it is intended to be a conservative production improvement and is guarded behind feature flagging for controlled rollout.
